title: PG&E and SDG&E Approve SolarEdge Nexis Meter Collar, Simplifying Home Backup Installations Across California
body_markdown:
*Approved in PG&E and SDG&E territories with SCE witness testing scheduled, the purpose-built meter collar takes hardware, labor and a truck full of extra parts out of residential battery backup jobs*


**MILPITAS, Calif. — October 20, 2026 —** SolarEdge Technologies, Inc., a global leader in smart energy technology, today announced that its SolarEdge Nexis IslandDER™ meter collar has been approved for use in the service territories of Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) and San Diego Gas and Electric (SDG&E), with Southern California Edison (SCE) scheduled to complete witness testing. Installers now have a single solution approved across the state.


The approvals come as battery adoption continues to rise in California, where the cost of installing home backup is driven by a structural feature of the state’s housing stock. Meter-main combination panels are widespread and lack the physical space conventional backup components require. In practice, a California backup installation without a meter collar involves electrical work to move loads. Combined with SolarEdge Nexis support for both DC- and AC-coupled configurations, the approved meter collar gives installers greater flexibility across retrofit and new-build projects.


"This approval by California's major utilities unlocks the full value of the SolarEdge Nexis platform for installers and homeowners across the state," said Amir Cohen, General Manager, SolarEdge North America. "As battery adoption grows, simplifying backup installation becomes increasingly important. By consolidating hardware at the meter socket and helping homeowners avoid costly panel upgrades, we're making the cost and complexity of a backup installation far lower, on every backup job in the state."


Developed in collaboration with ConnectDER, the SolarEdge Nexis IslandDER™ meter collar consolidates key backup and system control functions into a single unit installed behind the utility billing meter. This eliminates the need for backup loads panel, separate system controller and circuit relocations a conventional installation requires.


While analog meter collars require a separate hardwired communication cable to be run and commissioned on site, SolarEdge Nexis IslandDER™ communicates digitally with the SolarEdge Nexis Inverter over a standard Ethernet connection—


a cable already on every truck, with no custom part to source or special termination to get right.


*"The IslandDER meter collar makes the interconnection process a lot simpler, and paired with SolarEdge Nexis it keeps the whole installation clean and straightforward,"* said Zachary Hood, Director of Residential Construction at Stellar Solar.


*"Anything that lets us put in solar and storage more efficiently is a win for our crews and for the homeowner."*


The meter collar is a standard component in all SolarEdge Nexis installations that include battery backup. The platform combines inverter, battery storage and energy management in a compact system, with Simple-Click™ battery blocks that stack without wiring between units, storage scaling from 5kWh to 80kWh*, up to 13kW on-grid and 14.5kW in backup, and 185 Locked Rotor Amps to start large appliances such as HVAC systems.


SolarEdge Nexis also includes Power Control System (PCS) capabilities that help qualifying homeowners avoid costly main service panel upgrades.


SolarEdge Nexis and SolarEdge Nexis IslandDER™ are available for purchase through distribution nationwide. California installers can access configuration and interconnection documentation at the


[Installer InfoCenter](https://marketing.solaredge.com/solaredge-nexis-infocenter-en-1ph) , accessible from the


[SolarEdge Nexis webpage](https://www.solaredge.com/us/installers/nexis-for-installers) . California is the largest market in the North American rollout of SolarEdge Nexis, the company's next-generation residential energy platform, which launched in the U.S. in July 2026 and has also begun rolling out in Germany, where it drew record order volumes.


* 4th battery stack support expected in Q1 2027.
